overall_summary: Crypto is under clear pressure today from hawkish Fed signals, rising yields, and a stronger dollar. Heavy Bitcoin ETF outflows and a retest of the 62K support add to the cautious tone, even after a brief lift from the Anthropic IPO news. Geopolitical tensions linger in the background without providing a decisive catalyst either way.
key_points: Hawkish FOMC minutes flag further rate hikes
Spot Bitcoin ETFs see another large outflow
BTC retests 62K support with long liquidations
Dollar and yields climb, pressuring risk assets
Iran and Middle East tensions remain elevated

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs See $306M Outflow, November Near $2.9B
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded another $306 million in net outflows on November 18, led by BlackRock's IBIT at about $149 million, following $240 million the day before. November outflows are approaching $2.9 billion and fund assets have dropped to a three-month low near $77.7 billion. Traders should care because sustained institutional redemptions remove a key demand pillar and add direct selling pressure into thin liquidity.
items.impact: Sustained selling pressure and weaker institutional bid

items.title: Hawkish FOMC Minutes Flag More Rate Hikes Ahead
items.summary: October FOMC minutes showed nearly all officials expect further rate increases to bring inflation back to target, with two members dissenting for an immediate hike and some open to more than 25 basis points in December if data worsens. Bitcoin slid toward $62,500 on the release amid higher yields and dollar strength. This matters because higher-for-longer rates tighten liquidity and historically weigh on risk assets like Bitcoin.
items.impact: Macro headwind raising odds of further downside tests

items.title: Anthropic Record $107B IPO Lifts Bitcoin Off $62K Lows
items.summary: Anthropic priced its Nasdaq debut at $83 a share, raising about $81 billion publicly plus a $26 billion private placement for a total near $107 billion, the largest IPO on record, with a $1.5 trillion valuation. Nasdaq futures jumped and Bitcoin rebounded from overnight lows near $62,000 back toward $64,000. Ripple's CEO said the pre-IPO liquidity drain mirrored SpaceX and expects a post-listing crypto rally. Traders watch whether risk appetite returns once the capital raise is complete.
items.impact: Potential risk-on bounce if IPO debuts strongly

items.title: Binance Wins $6.5B Freezing Order on Hack Recovery
items.summary: Binance secured a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order from Abu Dhabi Global Market courts targeting assets from its October $6.3 billion hack attributed to North Korean actors. Roughly $2.85 billion or about 45 percent has already been frozen or intercepted by partners including stablecoin issuers. The order gives legal cover for returns and updates a list of 26,000 wallets. This reduces exchange counterparty risk fears after the largest crypto theft on record.
items.impact: Supports exchange confidence without immediate price catalyst

items.title: CoinShares Sells All ETH Treasury, Half SOL for Buyback
items.summary: Digital asset manager CoinShares liquidated its entire corporate Ethereum treasury and half its Solana holdings in October, raising $19.3 million to help fund a board-approved $40 million share repurchase program. It retained its Bitcoin position. CEO Jean-Marie Mognetti framed it as capital discipline favoring the company's own stock over idle treasury tokens. The sales add minor supply to ETH and SOL during a weak market but signal selective conviction.

items.title: Bitcoin Retests $62K Support Amid Heavy Long Liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin dipped to $62,000 for the second time this week before bouncing, with hundreds of millions in liquidations over 24 hours, the majority long positions, as Fear and Greed hit extreme levels near 10. Open interest and funding pointed to short or hedged positioning while stablecoin supply contracted. Traders care because a confirmed hold of this support after the washout could spark short covering, while a break opens lower targets.
items.impact: Key technical level; resolution decides next directional move

items.title: FOMC Minutes Signal Broad Support for December Hike
items.summary: Minutes from the Fed's late-October meeting show nearly all officials expect further rate increases will be needed to bring inflation back to target, with the October hold described by some as a close call. Two members dissented for an immediate quarter-point hike, and a couple floated the possibility of a half-point move in December if data stayed hot. Markets already price a December hike at roughly ninety-five percent odds. Crypto traders should care because higher-for-longer policy tightens financial conditions and typically pressures risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: Solidifies December hike bets and higher yields, weighing on BTC and equities

items.title: US Dollar Hits Fresh 19-Month High on Hawkish Fed
items.summary: The dollar index climbed to its strongest level since April twenty twenty-five, briefly nearing one hundred four, as FOMC minutes and Fed speak reinforced expectations for more rate hikes. It eased slightly after a seven-session rally but stayed elevated near multi-month highs. A stronger greenback makes dollar-denominated assets like Bitcoin more expensive for foreign buyers and often coincides with risk-off flows. Traders watch DXY for confirmation of the higher-rates regime.
items.impact: Strong USD headwind for crypto and other risk assets

items.title: Fed's Waller Pushes for Fifty Basis Point December Hike
items.summary: Influential Fed Governor Christopher Waller called for a more aggressive response to sticky inflation, arguing a half-point hike in December or a clear signal of faster future tightening may be needed. His comments came alongside the hawkish minutes and helped cement market pricing for at least a quarter-point move next month. This keeps the higher-for-longer narrative alive and supports the dollar and yields. Crypto markets tend to dislike unexpected hawkish shocks from voting members.
items.impact: Raises odds of larger or faster tightening, negative for risk appetite

items.title: Treasury Yields Hold Elevated Near Five Percent
items.summary: The ten-year Treasury yield hovered around five point zero five to five point one percent, with two-year yields near four point eight percent, after the hawkish minutes and Waller comments. Yields dipped at times on auction demand and softer oil but remain high by recent standards. Elevated real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like Bitcoin and tighten financial conditions across markets. Watch for any break higher as a fresh catalyst for risk-off moves.
items.impact: Higher yields compete with crypto and pressure valuations

items.title: Housing Starts Rebound but Permits Plunge on High Rates
items.summary: October housing starts jumped nine point nine percent to one point three zero nine million annualized, beating forecasts, driven partly by multifamily. Building permits, however, dropped seven point four percent to one point two nine five million, the weakest in years, with single-family permits hitting multi-year lows. High mortgage rates above seven percent continue to squeeze future construction and affordability. This mixed data shows the economy is still feeling the bite of tight policy, supporting the Fed's inflation fight narrative.
items.impact: Confirms rate sensitivity in housing without derailing growth outlook

items.title: Jobless Claims and Philly Fed Due; Labor Still Tight
items.summary: Today's key data releases are initial jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey at eight thirty Eastern. Prior claims held near two hundred thousand, historically low and consistent with a resilient labor market. Consensus looks for claims around one ninety-seven to two hundred thousand and Philly Fed near twenty. Soft claims would ease rate fears while hot data would reinforce the hawkish Fed path. Crypto traders treat these as real-time checks on whether the economy is cooling enough for the Fed to pause.
items.impact: Data surprise could swing near-term rate odds and risk sentiment

items.title: Trump, Xi, Putin Hold First-Ever Trilateral Summit
items.summary: US President Trump, China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Putin met for the first time as a trio on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen. They discussed nuclear arms control, the wars in Ukraine and Iran, trade, and keeping oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz. Trump called it history-making and voiced optimism on Ukraine and barring Iranian nukes, with China issuing a peace declaration, but no major concrete deals emerged and expectations stayed low. Traders should watch for any de-escalation signals that could ease risk premiums or shift great-power dynamics.
items.impact: Potential risk-on relief if peace talks advance, otherwise status-quo volatility

items.title: Trump Weighs Fresh Strikes as US-Iran Clashes Persist
items.summary: Reports say President Trump is considering another round of extensive strikes on Iran, with Netanyahu pushing for a multi-day campaign, while tit-for-tat attacks continue in the Gulf including on shipping and bases in Kuwait and Bahrain. Iran warned neighbors against hosting US forces and claimed tanker incidents in Hormuz. Oil steadied after a sharp drop as markets balance escalation risks against recovering supplies. This keeps a heavy geopolitical risk premium on energy and risk assets.
items.impact: Heightened oil volatility and risk-off pressure on crypto and equities

items.title: IEA: Iran War Is Largest Energy Security Threat Ever
items.summary: The International Energy Agency released its outlook declaring the Middle East crisis sparked by the Iran conflict the biggest threat to energy security in history, dwarfing the 1970s oil shocks. It cites massive cumulative supply losses and says the energy world will never fully return to pre-war patterns, with lasting shifts toward diversification, renewables, nuclear and reduced Hormuz dependence. Longer disruption means deeper structural change. Energy traders and macro desks must price in permanent higher security costs and accelerated energy transition.
items.impact: Long-term support for alternatives but short-term oil and inflation uncertainty

items.title: Ukraine Hits Kerch Bridge Rail Section Third Time This Week
items.summary: Ukrainian forces struck the railway section of the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Crimea overnight, suspending train traffic in the third attack in days after earlier damage collapsed a road span. Ukraine called it a hit on a key Russian supply artery for ammunition and fuel; Russia reported temporary halt and planned quick repairs. The timing came hours before Putin sat down with Trump and Xi. It underscores the grinding war continues even amid high-level diplomacy and could complicate any quick settlement talks.
items.impact: Sustains war-related risk premium without immediate directional catalyst

items.title: Israel Completes Rare Gaza Raid Beyond Yellow Line
items.summary: Israeli forces ended a tank and troop operation in central Gaza west of the Yellow Line ceasefire boundary, saying they dismantled a Hamas terror tunnel that threatened troops. It was the highest-profile ground incursion across the line since the 2025 truce, with evacuation orders, road closures and some reported casualties; Hamas called it a flagrant violation. The main north-south road later reopened. Fragile ceasefire strains in Gaza add another layer of Middle East instability for markets already watching Iran.
items.impact: Minor escalation risk that could feed broader regional risk-off sentiment

items.title: Europe Rallies Ukraine Support Amid Trump-Putin Talks
items.summary: European leaders from Germany, France, Britain and others met in Berlin with NATO's chief and US envoys as a show of support for Ukraine, while the EU advanced a roughly 45-50 billion euro loan package for Kyiv's 2027 needs. The gathering comes as Trump meets Putin and Xi, raising European fears that decisions on the war could bypass them. Russia continued strikes on Ukraine. This highlights the split between US diplomacy and European commitment, affecting aid flows and longer-term war outlook.
items.impact: Supports Ukraine funding stability but underscores alliance frictions
